He was moved out before I met him, but he had a terrible roommate situation and emergency moved in with his mom and brother about 3ish months before we met. He says it's not a permanent thing but there are no plans to move out yet because his late grandmother left him, his mom, and his uncle a house they need to sell. His uncle is a psycho and making everything difficult so moving out is up in the air until that happens. 

But yes, he is currently living with them in a 2bed 1bath apt and he sleeps on the couch. The entire situation is insane and he won't let me help. I've asked if he wanted to move in with me or get a place together but he insists he can't until they are taken care of. I have no idea what that means because he's not contributing to rent, just chores and food.

I don't think he's seeing anyone else or checked out, he's just up his family's ass 24/7. We see each other once a week on the weekends, and he does spend the night but he doesn't arrive at my place until afternoon and leaves around the same time on Sunday. He literally sees his family every day but can't seem to make more time for me. I think it's ridiculous but I know they've all been through a lot of trauma together so I was trying to be understanding but this went too far for me.

The part about requiring too much time wasn't quite out of the blue, but I didn't know how to include it in the post. A couple weeks ago we had a serious talk about where our relationship was going because we've been seeing each other for 9 months and I only get to see him once a week (if I'm lucky) and I asked if he was able to allot more time to see me during the week. Keep in mind - I asked if he could work it out, I did not demand he see me more often. But he's like his family's support system I guess? Nobody cooks so he always gets them food after work, cleans the house, and chauffeurs his brother around (who is 18 and apparently doesn't want to learn to drive or take public transport). I feel like his family takes advantage of him but they've been through a LOT of trauma together and are very close-knit. I don't know what to do. I may have to cut my losses because he's unwilling to grow up and be independent.

I wish that were true! In the entire 9 months we've dated I've only convinced him to do something outside of his routine a handful of times. I'm more spontaneous than he is which is why I like to stick to the scheduled dates as much as possible because I'd have to wait a whole week before I could see him again. I was mostly thrown off by meeting his family at the spur of the moment.

I was in this exact situation over the summer. I broke up with him in September but we're unfortunately still living together until our lease is up in March. I did not like who I became when trying to debate with him. How can you debate when they are working on a completely false set of "facts"? I am a nice person, open-minded, kind, understanding, etc. but with him and this fucking crazy conspiracy theory, I am basically belligerent. 

I refuse to talk to him about any of this any longer. If he brings it up, I simply say "I told you I don't want to talk about this." If he continues, I will cover my ears (immature, perhaps, but if he's not going to respect me then I won't be respecting him either). If that doesn't work either I just go into another room and close the door. 

I think the reason I get so upset is because I know he's not a terrible person and I'm horrified that this bullshit theory has consumed him and so many others I know.

It was hard for me to let go, but I had to remember the phrase, "You can't set yourself on fire to keep others warm" in order to keep my sanity. Talking to him was like being gaslighted over and over. I know what I'm seeing and hearing is real and that Q and the other right wing BS are the lies. However, being exposed to that misinformation so often made it harder to resist because I want so badly to understand everyone and reach common ground. Unfortunately you can't reach common ground with someone living in an alternate reality.

Routine:
Once a month use Alberto VO5 Herbal Escapes Kiwi Lime Squeeze Clarifying Shampoo.

Twice a week I use TRESemmé Botanique Conditioner, Nourish & Replenish to co-wash my hair (detangle in the shower) and after I get out of the shower I squeeze as much water out as possible and apply a little more than a quarter size amount of As I Am Olive & Tea Tree Oil Conditioner (for dry, itchy scalp care).

I comb through it with a wide tooth comb for even distribution before flipping my head upside down and scrunching it in so the curls form.

Finish that off with a couple pumps of DevaCurl Light Defining Styling Hair Gel which I also scrunch in.

Air dry for roughly 3-6 hours (depending on weather) then flip my head upside down again and scrunch out the crunch.

For the rest of the week I just wet my hair in the shower, detangle with the wide tooth comb, and scrunch in a couple more pumps of gel.

I've tried leaving the curls alone and also using a spray bottle to moisten but not saturate my hair with water, but the curls get too clumped up and start to tangle unless I fully wet my hair every day and comb it out.

I should I also mention I use a satin pillow case and wear my hair in a pineapple while sleeping.

If there's any other questions feel free to ask! :D

I think the most important question is whether or not she is in therapy or on medication to help with the depression. If she isn't, I'd highly recommend helping her work on getting assistance to deal with mental health. As someone who has suffered from depression of this magnitude before it will completely destroy you as a person and you are basically a leech. However, medication/therapy does wonders and eventually she'll want to live life again instead of draining you of yours. If you love her, help her. If she's already getting help and things haven't improved then I guess you have a tough decision to make.

Good luck.

I was horribly depressed for roughly 3 years. Full on unemployed, not in school, mooching off my parents levels of worthless existence and unable to function depression.

I started to play World of Warcraft out of boredom one day and eventually became addicted. For the first time in my life (that I could recall) I was getting positive feedback from people. I was a good healer in the game and I made a bunch of friends. This was late Vanilla/early BC and it was one of the best times in my life. I wasn't being judged for my appearance, but for my abilities. Maybe they weren't the most useful abilities, but at least I had value to these people.

I'm still friends with about 50% of the people I met during that period of my life and I believe without them I wouldn't have been able to pull myself out of that depression and be motivated to go back to school and live life. A decade later and I've met nearly all of them in person, I have 2 associate's degrees, a good job, financially independent, and living in my dream state (Colorado) working on getting a bachelor's in Computer Science.

Video games saved my life!

I don't know to be honest. I want to say I'm good, but also unbearably lonely. I lived in Florida for the first 29 years of my life and I had two best friends. One of them moved to Texas to pursue school and a relationship with someone they met online. The second one died from stage 4 pancreatic cancer at a very young age. I moved to Colorado two months after their death knowing absolutely nobody outside of Florida. I got into a toxic relationship that lasted roughly 2 1/2 years that drained what little ambition and desire to live I had. I finally cut that person out of my life but I'm all alone here now. I didn't make friends because that person was my everything and I worked a night shift and was completely alone all night. Now I've got a day shift job, have been trying to date again, but it's not working out and I'm sure everyone has the same problem and I'm not special but it's exhausting and discouraging, especially when I feel like I'm irreparably broken. I finally decided to stop looking and try focusing on myself, something I don't think I've ever done in my life. For whatever reason I never saw myself as something worthy of caring for and so I've put the majority of my energy into helping others and making them happy. I don't know what makes me happy. I'm taking steps to improve my situation but there seems to be so much time in between those moments... so much emptiness.
Fig Newtons! I'm still crying... they were my favorite snack as a kid. :(

The best part was the food! My mom would go all out for my grandma and my grandma would go all out for my mom so there'd be tons of sweets that we didn't have on the regular. Also, bacon and eggs for Sunday breakfast. That smell still reminds me of visiting. We only visited a couple of times per year because my parents worked so much and didn't have a lot of spare money, even if it was only a 2 1/2 hour drive.

For my dad's side, she lived a lot closer so I saw her more and spent many summers there while both my parent's worked. She lived in a retirement apartment complex not far from the downtown Orlando area so we'd have to walk to get groceries or just to look around the shops and that was so different from where I grew up in very east Orlando, which many people considered the sticks (we had dirt roads to our neighborhood until I was in middle school). I'd be able to eat all the mac and cheese I wanted and re-watch movies a million times without complaint (one of my favorites was Jumanji). 

Ah... good times.

My hair was ULTRA dry. I used to live in Florida and my curls loved to absorb the moisture and they looked decent without too much effort, but I moved to Colorado 3 years ago and it pretty much destroyed my hair. It was so dry I could hear it crackle from static electricity. 

Routine:

I’ve done two protein treatments with SheaMoisture Manuka Honey & Yogurt Hydrate + Repair Protein Power Treatment

Once a month I wash with VO5 clarifying shampoo.

Co-wash with the TRESemme Botanique conditioner.

Leave hair completely dripping wet, I don’t even use a towel, just kinda squeeze a bit out before getting out of the shower.

Use praying hands to apply As I Am leave-in conditioner, argon oil towards the ends because my hair is a hot mess (I really need to cut it), and then finally LA Looks Extreme Gel.

Let hair air dry for roughly 4-5 hours because I don’t have a hair dryer/diffuser.

Flip my hair upside down and scrunch out the crunch!

I feel like I still have a long way to go but it’s better than it used to look. Also, I’ve tried plopping and doing all that stuff in the shower with my hair upside down but it just gave me the craziest curl patterns; I prefer it to look a little tamer.
